question: Does a geometry-leading clock make the predicted endpoint physically informative before the event commits, without degrading unguided joint generation?
motivation: geoinfo-1.1 check B (PR #110): under the sync clock xTB on x1_hat becomes informative only at t~0.7, after 85% of events commit (NO_USABLE_WINDOW)
reused_definitions: check_b_time_window: generator, seeds, 32 proposals per parent per seed, namespace, grid, signals, targets, within-parent Spearman, t_geo, window_fraction and its 0.20 threshold, bond-change-set commit sensitivity
data_scope: V1a development parents only (62 parents, 21 formula groups); no screen or M0 val/test parents

paths.sync: t_b = s, t_x = s (rerun under this code; must reproduce check B)

axis: every time is the integration parameter s, which equals t_x on all three paths; commit times and t_geo use the same s grid
pairing: same namespace and semantic noise keys, so each (parent, seed, proposal) starts from the same (b0, x0) on every path
primary: window_fraction of the xTB signal (x1_hat energy vs final event catalogue barrier) on each geometry-lead path

quality.comparison: path - sync, paired by parent, formula-cluster t two-sided 95% (xtbflow.v1.metrics.cluster_summary)
quality.tolerance: V1a baseline_check limits on point estimates: hits_best_reference drop <= 0.05 and valid-rate drop <= 0.10

reading.GEOMETRY_LEAD_OPENS_WINDOW: xTB window_fraction >= 0.20 and both quality drops within tolerance
reading.WINDOW_WITH_QUALITY_LOSS: xTB window_fraction >= 0.20 but a quality drop exceeds tolerance
reading.NO_USABLE_WINDOW: xTB window_fraction < 0.20, or the xTB signal is never informative
reading.per_path: each geometry-lead path gets its own reading; no path is chosen by its result here

reproduction_check: sync rerun vs the geoinfo-1.1 check B rows: share of trajectories with identical final event, proxy status and commit step (GPU batch nondeterminism up to ~2e-6 was measured in V1a, so near-1 rather than exact is expected)
numerics_note: predicted endpoints are recovered from float32 traces; on geometry_lead3 the first event increment is 8e-6, so b1_hat at the first steps carries ~1% relative error, which only matters before any event is decodable
